LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.

LACA is a new database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets from 134 species alongside their maximum lifespans, comprising over 148 million cells and 190 annotated cell types. It enables cross-species comparisons of cellular and molecular programs associated with longevity and aging, filling a gap in resources that link single-cell expression profiles to species lifespan.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-19 Medium

PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.

PRGdb 5.0 is a major update to the Plant Resistance Genes database, now covering 279 plant proteomes with 874,967 candidate resistance proteins, including 288,315 newly predicted ones. The curated reference set of experimentally supported resistance proteins more than doubled to 462, and the platform adds AI-assisted prioritization to complement domain-based classification. This provides a unified, expanded resource for discovering and exploring plant disease resistance genes.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-19 Medium

The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.

The mOTUs database has been updated to include a larger collection of 3.9 million genomes with functional annotations, improved coverage of understudied environments, and a new hierarchical environmental ontology with geographic coordinates for samples. This enables researchers to link microbial taxonomic composition to genome-encoded functional potential and biogeography across diverse environments, even when cultivated representative genomes are unavailable.

mSystems 2026-11-18 Medium

A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation.

The authors present a graph-based computational framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA-mRNA interactions, orthology relationships, and functional annotations across multiple bacterial species to enable comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation. This approach addresses the challenge that sRNAs often lack sequence conservation, allowing detection of functional conservation even when the underlying sequences have diverged or evolved independently.

CellStressDB: an AI-powered database of cellular responses to physical stressors.

CellStressDB is a new AI-powered database that compiles transcriptomic data on how cells respond to physical stressors, drawing from 131 studies covering over 2.3 million single-cell and 1,205 bulk samples across human and mouse. It organizes these data into 2,848 indexed analysis entries spanning nine stress classes and 21 tissue categories, providing a centralized resource for exploring stress-response programs.

A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.

This study performs a cell-type-resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation screen to identify gene expression changes that causally influence systemic lupus erythematosus and related immune phenotypes, moving beyond whole-blood averages that blur leukocyte-specific regulatory effects. The authors emphasise rigorous quality control of genetic instruments, allele orientation, and multiple-testing correction before interpreting biological signals.

PDBe in 2027: integrating literature annotations, molecular dynamics data, and AI-ready access.

PDBe has expanded its structural database by integrating residue-level annotations mined from more open-access literature, linking PDB structures to molecular dynamics simulations, and introducing AI-ready access formats. These updates make it easier for both researchers and computational tools to retrieve richly annotated structural data.

Computer methods and programs in biomedicine 2026-11-13 Medium

ONITH: An ontology-based non-clinical integration and term harmonization pipeline for data reuse in 3R.

ONITH is a pipeline that integrates non-clinical animal study data and harmonizes terminology using ontologies, aiming to make existing animal data more reusable in line with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace). By standardizing terms across heterogeneous sources, it supports data-driven drug development and offers a potential route to reduce reliance on new animal experiments.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-12 Medium

PANTHER: the protein tree and function resource in 2027.

PANTHER is a database of phylogenetic trees for protein-coding gene families, with branches manually annotated with Gene Ontology terms that model how protein functions evolved. These evolutionary models are used to propagate GO annotations to genes and to classify orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs. This paper reports updates to the resource since its 2022 publication.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-10 Medium

gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.

gcPathogen 2.0 expands a pathogen genomic surveillance database to 1,506 pathogenic species (bacteria, fungi, viruses, parasites) with over 2.3 million genomic records, now integrating transcriptional profiles and cross-habitat distribution tracking. The update also enables large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides, supporting One Health research across human, animal, and environmental reservoirs.

Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.

Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that supports standardized deposition of metabolomics data across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows, along with spectral resource management and online analysis tools. It contains over 7.7 million reference spectra and adds disease-focused knowledge mining capabilities. The platform aims to make metabolomics data more findable, reusable, and analyzable in a single resource.

Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.

ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that combines network-based disease module identification with drug repurposing prediction, letting users interact with specialized AI agents through natural language. It aims to integrate fragmented algorithms and heterogeneous data sources into a single workflow, reducing the need for deep specialist expertise at each step. The work is presented as a platform development study rather than a validated biological discovery.

InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.

InterPro is a freely accessible database that integrates predictive models from multiple member databases to classify protein sequences into families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, and includes mappings to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe.

Plants (Basel, Switzerland) 2026-11-01 Medium

Functional Analysis of GarCIPK8 from Gossypium aridum Conferring Salt Stress Tolerance in Gossypium hirsutum.

The authors transferred GarCIPK8, a salt-responsive kinase gene from wild diploid cotton (Gossypium aridum), into cultivated upland cotton and found that overexpressing lines grew markedly better under high-salinity (300 mM NaCl) conditions. This suggests the CBL-CIPK signaling component GarCIPK8 can be used to improve salt tolerance in commercial cotton varieties.

Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.

This study profiled miRNA expression changes in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells after exposure to crystalline silica particles, identifying both intracellular and extracellular miRNA responses. The findings suggest that specific miRNAs could serve as biomarkers of silica exposure in human biomonitoring. The work is preliminary, with cytotoxicity assessment and dose-response profiling in a single cell line.

Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.

This review synthesizes evidence on managing symptoms of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a knowledge graph for nursing interventions. It addresses the lack of structured clinical tools by organizing GVHD symptom management across organ systems into a knowledge map. The work aims to support nurses in delivering more systematic, evidence-based care.

The Journal of investigative dermatology 2026-11-01 Medium

Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.

This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of the skin bacterium Cutibacterium acnes rapidly trigger extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 T cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved protein profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps showed distinct proteome programs depending on the C. acnes strain, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in acne pathogenesis.

Comparative Transcriptomic and Physiological Profiling Reveals Species-Associated Differences Across Five Duckweed Species.

The authors generated de novo transcriptome assemblies for five duckweed species grown under identical conditions and compared them alongside physiological measurements, using BUSCO to assess assembly completeness. This provides a baseline resource characterizing molecular and physiological differences among species, useful for selecting duckweeds for biomass or phytoremediation applications.

A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.

This paper develops a focused knowledge graph that organizes Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with emotional comorbidities (anxiety, depression, insomnia), linking syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs to their sources. It then evaluates the graph's contribution to generated answers through a blinded question-answering assessment. The work shows how a domain-specific knowledge graph can support grounded, source-attributed QA in TCM.

Poultry science 2026-10-28 Medium

Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.

This study used a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning methods (Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine) to identify SNP markers associated with body weight in broiler chickens at hatch and 3 weeks of age. The work demonstrates that GBS plus ML can serve as a cheaper alternative to high-density SNP arrays for genome-wide association studies in poultry breeding. It provides a practical framework for resource-limited breeding programs to discover informative markers for economically important traits.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-27 Medium

Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.

The authors compute phenologs—pairs of human diseases and model-organism phenotypes whose associated genes overlap more than expected by chance after orthology mapping—at knowledge-graph scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph, covering human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families to control for orthology, they produce a catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases, including cross-species links such as mouse-to-slime-mold. This provides a systematic, principled resource for transferring gene-phenotype knowledge from model organisms to human disease.

OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.

OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that converts literature on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable evidence records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and auditable.

Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.

This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware Transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict acute kidney injury before onset and to forecast patient prognosis after diagnosis. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data that challenge conventional machine learning methods. The work suggests that attention-based deep learning with biomarker integration can support both prevention and post-onset care decisions in AKI.

Computational and structural biotechnology journal 2026-01-01 Medium

Dingent: A Configurable Agent Framework for Biological Database Retrieval and Integration.

Dingent is an open-source agent framework that lets developers expose biological database functions as tools, which administrators then compose into explicit multistep retrieval workflows that users can query in natural language. It integrates data-access plugins, configurable assistants, directed workflows, and web interfaces, and was benchmarked against a single-assistant tool-calling approach. The work aims to make cross-database biological data retrieval more reproducible and configurable.

Frontiers in neuroergonomics 2026-01-01 Low

Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states.

This hypothesis paper proposes a framework for 'closed-loop cognitive state control,' in which an individual's task-specific high-performance cognitive states are estimated in real time from multimodal behavioral, physiological, and contextual signals and then actively stabilized or recovered. The authors frame cognition as a partially observable dynamical system, positioning this as a neuroengineering objective rather than a tested intervention. No empirical results are reported; the contribution is conceptual.
